regulations.primary_reference: Approved Document K (Protection from Falling, Collision and Impact)

formula_2R_G.note: 2 × riser + going should sit in this range for comfort

commercial_category_1.contrast_nosings: required per Doc M accessibility guidance

regulations.glass_balustrade: Toughened or toughened-laminated safety glass required. Reference BS 6180 for balustrade design and BS 6262 for glazing.
regulations.loft_conversion_exception: Alternating tread stair permitted where a full compliant stair will not fit, only for access to a single habitable room.
regulations.building_control: New staircases and significant alterations trigger Building Control notification in England/Wales. Scotland uses Building Standards; NI uses Building Regulations (Northern Ireland).

regional_regulations_variance.england: Approved Document K (2013 edition currently active)
regional_regulations_variance.wales: Approved Document K adopted with Welsh amendments
regional_regulations_variance.scotland: Building Standards (Section 4: Safety, Standard 4.3 Stairs and Ramps) — different specific values
regional_regulations_variance.northern_ireland: Building Regulations (Northern Ireland) — mirrors Doc K in most respects with local wording

victorian_terrace.notes: Original stairs often steep by modern standards. Renovation more common than replacement. Paired-neighbour mirror rule applies (right-side house typically has staircase on left).

1930s_semi.notes: Straight or quarter-turn typical. Original oak or pine stairs frequently intact.

modern_new_build.notes: Straight pine + MDF riser default. Prime candidate for oak refurbishment upgrade.

georgian_townhouse.notes: Grand proportions. Classic period style dominates. Restoration typically preferred over replacement.

cottage.notes: Often steep and narrow. Farmhouse style. May be non-compliant with current Doc K — retained under listed-building or historic exemption.

apartment.notes: Rarely has an internal staircase; where present, often to a mezzanine or roof terrace.

cultural_preferences: Oak is the default premium timber choice — customer defaults to oak unless steered otherwise.
Glass balustrade increasingly common in mid-to-premium new builds; still associated with 'modern'.
Renovation preferred over replacement in period properties.
Painted string + oak tread is a classic UK budget-to-mid combination.
'Building regulations' is a household phrase — customers know Doc K exists even if they don't cite it.
common_customer_journey: Compare 3-5 companies by website + Google reviews
regulatory_warnings: Doc K sets MINIMUMS, not maximums.
Retrofitting a stair into an existing opening often triggers Building Control notification even if the original was legal.
Wales, Scotland and NI have their own versions of Building Regulations — never quote England Doc K to a Scottish customer as if it applies.
Historic listed buildings may retain non-compliant original stairs — do not modify without listed-building consent.
